goal: etl.sql runs top to bottom with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1` on source tables built from source/schema.sql and source/seed.py plus dashboard_schema.sql; it reconciles exactly as etl_spec.md defines (source order count minus loaded order count is 0, recorded in etl_run_log); running it twice gives the same dashboard row counts; both dashboard tables are non-empty; and it handles the cases etl_spec.md §5 describes (multi-category orders and completed orders without lines).
final_message:
`etl.sql` is done. It runs cleanly with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1` on a fresh build from `source/schema.sql`, the seeder and `dashboard_schema.sql`. Both runs on that build logged 50,000 source orders, 50,000 loaded and a mismatch of 0. The second run produced identical results (80 category rows, 128 country rows).

**How it works**
- **One category per order:** each COMPLETED order is assigned its controlling category, the category of its lowest-`order_item_id` line. `order_count` is then a count of distinct orders per month and category, so every completed order is counted exactly once.
- **Orders with no lines** go under a `'(no items)'` category instead of being dropped. A first line whose product can't be found would go under `'(unknown product)'`.
- **Country rollup:** revenue is quantity × unit price summed over every line of a COMPLETED order. A customer whose completed order has no lines still counts toward `customer_count`.
- **Rerunnable:** each run empties the two dashboard tables and reloads them in one transaction, so nothing is double-counted. `etl_run_log` gains exactly one row per run.
- **Consistent counts:** the whole run reads one snapshot of the source tables, so the load and the source count agree even if orders are being written at the same time.
- **Months are computed in UTC.** The result doesn't depend on the time zone of whoever runs it; an order at 23:30 New York time on Jan 31 lands in February.
- **If the mismatch isn't 0:** the load is undone, so the dashboard keeps its last good contents. The failed run is still recorded in `etl_run_log` with its mismatch, and psql exits with an error.

**Fixes along the way**
- My first version picked each order's first line with a per-order lookup. With no index on `order_items.order_id`, that took about 94 seconds. A single sort over `order_items` brought it down to about 0.17 seconds.
- psql doesn't substitute its variables inside a `DO $$…$$` block, so the failure message now gets its values through a session setting.

**Tests (`tests/test_etl.sh`, all passing):** the seed gives every order exactly one line, so neither §5 case occurs in the sample data. The script rebuilds everything and adds test orders:
- a completed order spanning three categories, with lines inserted out of id order;
- a completed order with no lines;
- a pending order spanning two categories (must be ignored);
- an order near midnight, run with a New York session time zone.

It checks rerun stability, the reconciliation formula and both dashboard tables against a separately written calculation. It also breaks the order counting on purpose and confirms the ETL exits with an error, leaves the dashboard unchanged and logs the bad mismatch (−81).

**Decision for you: category revenue.** The spec contradicts itself here. §4.1 and §5.1 say category `revenue`/`units_sold` come from the order's controlling line only. §5.1 also calls this the order's "full contribution". I followed the explicit rule, so other categories' lines in a multi-category order are left out of the category view. On the seed data this changes nothing, because every order has one line. With the test orders, category revenue is 23.00 lower than country revenue. Each run prints this gap. If finance expects the two views to total the same, the alternative is to credit the order's whole line revenue to its controlling category. That's a one-line change, but it departs from the spec's wording.
output_text:
### FILE: etl.sql
```
-- ============================================================================
-- R5 ETL: source (orders, order_items, products, customers) -> dashboard
--
--   psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f etl.sql
--
-- Implements etl_spec.md:
--   * dash_revenue_by_category : month x controlling-category rollup (§2, §4.1, §5.1)
--   * dash_revenue_by_country  : month x country rollup                (§4.2)
--   * etl_run_log              : one reconciliation row per run        (§4.3, §5.2)
--
-- Design notes
--   * Idempotent: full refresh (TRUNCATE + INSERT) inside one transaction, so a
--     rerun replaces the dashboard rather than appending to it. Only
--     etl_run_log grows, by exactly one row per run, as the spec requires.
--   * Consistent snapshot: the transaction runs at REPEATABLE READ, so the
--     loads and the reconciliation's source count all see the same source
--     data even while orders are being written concurrently.
--   * Month buckets are computed in UTC (order_date is timestamptz), so the
--     result does not depend on the TimeZone setting of the session that runs it.
--   * Hard gate (§5.2): when mismatch <> 0 the load is rolled back (the
--     dashboard keeps its last good state), the failed run is still recorded in
--     etl_run_log with its signed mismatch, and the script exits with an error.
-- ============================================================================

\set ON_ERROR_STOP 1

BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
SET LOCAL TimeZone = 'UTC';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Order grain: every COMPLETED order, exactly once, with its controlling line
-- (lowest order_item_id) and its controlling category. Orders without lines
-- and lines without a joinable product get sentinel categories so that no
-- COMPLETED order is ever dropped (§5.2).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The controlling line is chosen set-based (DISTINCT ON over one sort/hash of
-- order_items) rather than with a per-order correlated LIMIT 1 subquery: the
-- source has no index on order_items.order_id, and a correlated lookup
-- degenerates into one order_items scan per order (quadratic).
CREATE TEMP TABLE etl_completed_order ON COMMIT DROP AS
WITH controlling_line AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (oi.order_id)
           oi.order_id, oi.order_item_id, oi.product_id, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price
    FROM   order_items oi
    JOIN   orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.status = 'COMPLETED'
    ORDER  BY oi.order_id, oi.order_item_id
)
SELECT o.order_id,
       o.customer_id,
       to_char(o.order_date, 'YYYY-MM')                      AS month,
       CASE
           WHEN cl.order_item_id IS NULL THEN '(no items)'
           WHEN p.product_id    IS NULL THEN '(unknown product)'
           ELSE p.category
       END                                                   AS category,
       COALESCE(cl.quantity * cl.unit_price, 0)::numeric     AS controlling_revenue,
       COALESCE(cl.quantity, 0)                              AS controlling_units
FROM   orders o
LEFT   JOIN controlling_line cl ON cl.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT   JOIN products p ON p.product_id = cl.product_id
WHERE  o.status = 'COMPLETED';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. dash_revenue_by_category  (§4.1)
--    One row per (month, controlling category). order_count counts DISTINCT
--    orders; revenue/units_sold come from each order's controlling line.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRUNCATE dash_revenue_by_category;

INSERT INTO dash_revenue_by_category (month, category, revenue, order_count, units_sold)
SELECT month,
       category,
       SUM(controlling_revenue),
       COUNT(DISTINCT order_id),
       SUM(controlling_units)
FROM   etl_completed_order
GROUP  BY month, category;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. dash_revenue_by_country  (§4.2)
--    Revenue = SUM(quantity * unit_price) over all lines of COMPLETED orders.
--    Line-less COMPLETED orders contribute 0 revenue but their customer still
--    counts as a (distinct) customer for that month/country.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TRUNCATE dash_revenue_by_country;

INSERT INTO dash_revenue_by_country (month, country, revenue, customer_count)
SELECT co.month,
       c.country,
       COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0),
       COUNT(DISTINCT co.customer_id)
FROM   etl_completed_order co
JOIN   customers c        ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
LEFT   JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id  = co.order_id
GROUP  BY co.month, c.country;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Reconciliation  (§5.2) — formula exactly as specified.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT now()                         AS etl_started_at,
       s.source_order_count          AS etl_source_order_count,
       l.loaded_order_count          AS etl_loaded_order_count,
       s.source_order_count - l.loaded_order_count AS etl_mismatch,
       (s.source_order_count - l.loaded_order_count = 0)::int AS etl_reconciled
FROM   (SELECT COUNT(*) AS source_order_count
        FROM   orders WHERE status = 'COMPLETED') s,
       (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(order_count), 0) AS loaded_order_count
        FROM   dash_revenue_by_category) l
\gset

\if :etl_reconciled
    INSERT INTO etl_run_log (started_at, finished_at, source_order_count,
                             loaded_order_count, mismatch)
    VALUES (:'etl_started_at', clock_timestamp(), :etl_source_order_count,
            :etl_loaded_order_count, :etl_mismatch);

    -- Informational: the category view carries controlling-line revenue only
    -- (§4.1/§5.1), so it is expected to be <= the country view's line revenue.
    DO $$
    DECLARE
        cat_rev numeric; ctry_rev numeric; cat_rows bigint; ctry_rows bigint;
    BEGIN
        SELECT COALESCE(SUM(revenue), 0), COUNT(*) INTO cat_rev,  cat_rows  FROM dash_revenue_by_category;
        SELECT COALESCE(SUM(revenue), 0), COUNT(*) INTO ctry_rev, ctry_rows FROM dash_revenue_by_country;
        RAISE NOTICE 'ETL reconciled: % category rows, % country rows; category revenue % vs country (all-lines) revenue % (non-controlling lines excluded from category view: %)',
            cat_rows, ctry_rows, cat_rev, ctry_rev, ctry_rev - cat_rev;
    END $$;

    COMMIT;
\else
    -- Gate failed: discard this load, keep the previous dashboard contents,
    -- record the failed run honestly, then exit non-zero.
    ROLLBACK;

    INSERT INTO etl_run_log (started_at, finished_at, source_order_count,
                             loaded_order_count, mismatch)
    VALUES (:'etl_started_at', clock_timestamp(), :etl_source_order_count,
            :etl_loaded_order_count, :etl_mismatch);

    -- psql variables are not interpolated inside dollar quotes; pass the
    -- message to the DO block through a session setting.
    SELECT set_config('etl.failure',
                      format('ETL reconciliation failed: mismatch = %s (source %s - loaded %s); load rolled back',
                             :'etl_mismatch', :'etl_source_order_count', :'etl_loaded_order_count'),
                      false) \g /dev/null
    DO $$ BEGIN
        RAISE EXCEPTION '%', current_setting('etl.failure');
    END $$;
\endif
```
